results.reason: The deliverable correctly calculates the long-stop date as 20 April 2026 (90 days after 20 January 2026), identifies the conflict with the expected merger clearance date of 4 June 2026, and recommends extending the conditions deadline to align with the regulatory timeline.

The deliverable accurately identifies that Clause 14.2 of the Fenwick Holdings Ltd contract permits termination on change of control, that the Disclosure Letter Clause 3.1 incorrectly states no such provisions exist, and recommends obtaining consent as a condition precedent to Closing.

The deliverable identifies in Section 14.1 that the board meeting had only 2 directors present while Article 11 requires a quorum of three, notes the potential invalidity of the approval, and recommends a ratifying resolution.

The deliverable identifies the conflict between SPA Clause 9.7 (30 days) and Escrow Agreement Clause 5.2 (60 days) and recommends harmonising the notification periods, specifically proposing to increase the SPA period to 60 days.

The deliverable states the long-stop period is 90 days, correctly identifies the date as 20 April 2026, and the Time-Sensitive Obligations Summary table confirms 63 days remaining from the deliverable date of 16 February 2026.

While the deliverable identifies missing definitions and inconsistencies, it does not explain how each alternative reading of an ambiguous term would work in practice; it simply proposes standard definitions without exploring alternative interpretations.
Section 5 (Proposed Amendment Table) presents proposed changes in a clear before/after format with current text, proposed amendment, rationale, and risk level for each identified issue.
